solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Observe US policeman driven back by a conflagration

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something driven back is pushed the wrong way, so the letters run from right to left

parts.note: to espy is to catch sight of, to observe
an LA cop is a policeman in Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Someone watches an American cop being forced away from a raging fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The observing word and the Los Angeles cop are written together and then flipped as one, landing after the A: APOCALYPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocalypse is a catastrophic, world-ending destruction, and a huge all-consuming fire is one such cataclysm.

clue.text: They may advocate screening for privates

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for barristers, who plead cases in court
second meaning: short underpants that cover the private parts

explanation.surface: Lawyers may argue that private soldiers should be screened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privates' looks military but means the genitals; 'advocate' looks like a verb but describes what lawyers do. In Britain a brief is slang for a barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both courtroom lawyers who argue cases and a style of close-fitting underwear covering the groin.

clue.text: Recently established location for Oracle lacking introduction of prime capital

parts.note: something recently established is new

indicators.note: to be lacking something is to be without it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Delphi was the site of the most famous oracle of ancient Greece

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A newly set-up base for the Oracle software company lacks the touch of a prime capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oracle' looks like the software firm, but it is the Greek oracle at Delphi, which loses its P to become DELHI after NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: New Delhi is the capital city of India, the seat of its national government.

clue.text: Pleasure dome initially makes money

parts.note: fun is enjoyment or pleasure

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pleasure dome, like an amusement venue, starts out turning a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pleasure dome' reads as one thing (Coleridge's Xanadu), but it splits: the enjoyment word plus the dome's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fund is a sum of money set aside or collected for a purpose, so it stands for money.

clue.text: Hairy situation? Yes, and no

parts.note: surface reading: a hairy situation is a frightening near miss
setter's reading: a razor pass taken right down to the skin leaves the face with no hair at all

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a narrow escape (yes, hairy as in scary) and also a razor shave so near the skin that nothing hairy is left (no).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a narrow escape from danger is a scary, nerve-racking moment, which slang calls hairy.

clue.text: Men admitted to service bog

indicators.note: whoever is admitted goes inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: Mass is a church service
OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers are let into the latrine for duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog' is British slang for a toilet, which suits the barracks picture, but here it means a swamp. OR (other ranks) for men is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is an area of soft, waterlogged ground, a marsh or swamp, the same as a bog.

clue.text: Monitor first Revolutionary Guards

indicators.note: guards stand round what they protect, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: Lenin led the Russian Revolution
1st, with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A spy is told to watch the elite Revolutionary Guards first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary Guards' reads as Iran's military corps; split it, and the revolutionary is Lenin, who wraps round 1ST written with I for the one.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor a conversation or broadcast is to eavesdrop on or tune into it, which is what this phrase means.

clue.text: Poet releases capital payment

indicators.note: the capital is the head letter, and releasing it lets that opening letter go

parts.note: Dante Alighieri wrote the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A poet frees up some capital to make a payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks financial, which suits 'payment', but it means the first letter, here the D of the Italian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put into the pot before a poker hand, so it is a sum paid in advance.

clue.text: Desperately importunate Pole's interminable action

indicators.note: done desperately, things are thrown about wildly and end up out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A desperate, pestering Polish man keeps up his endless campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of the pushy Pole are rearranged; the apostrophe-s is just 'is' joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpetual motion is movement that never stops, the hypothetical machine running forever, so it is unending activity.

clue.text: Belief in revolution does perhaps lead to conspiracy

indicators.note: the lead is the front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: does are female deer; 'perhaps' marks them as an example

explanation.surface: Faith in an uprising may well breed a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb do; it is the plural of doe. The turned-round animals follow the first letter of the plot word.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of religious or political convictions, a system of faith someone holds.

clue.text: Demolish gloomy housing National Trust essentially neglected

indicators.note: a building that houses something holds it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: dismal means dreary or gloomy
the standard abbreviation; the National Trust looks after British historic houses

indicators.note: the essence is the very heart, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of this nine-letter word

explanation.surface: Pull down a dreary old house that the National Trust has let fall into neglect.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's stately home is the clue's best disguise: NT sits inside the gloomy word, then the centre of the neglected word ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle something is to take it apart piece by piece, which is to tear down or demolish it.

clue.text: US laboratory's mission to spread destruction

indicators.note: spreading out round something means stretching across it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: loss is ruin or destruction
the Alamo was a Spanish mission in Texas, site of the famous 1836 siege

explanation.surface: An American research lab's purpose is to cause widespread devastation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mission' looks like a task, which suits a weapons lab; it is the Texan mission building, wrapped in a word for destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Alamos National Laboratory in New Mexico is where the first atomic bombs were designed during the Manhattan Project.

clue.text: Invalid interpretation of note being circulated in Penny's absence

indicators.note: with someone absent they are missing, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a rumour being circulated is spreading

explanation.surface: A memo is passed round while Penny is away, and it gets misunderstood.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a colleague's name; it is P, the abbreviation for a penny, taken from the circulating word.
explanation.definitionFit: A misreading is a mistaken understanding of a text or situation, so it is a wrong interpretation.

clue.text: The cardinal points about current power source

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: south, north, east and west, the four compass points
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: The four compass directions point towards an electrical power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current power source' reads as electricity; split it, and current is I, slipped into the compass letters. Sinews are a source of muscular power.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is tendon, and figuratively strength or vigour, the thing that gives muscles their pulling force.

clue.text: Damaged old scars will regularly crack

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first and third letters

explanation.surface: Damaged old scars will keep splitting open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a verb about the scars, but it is the adjective, as in a crack shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack performer is top-notch and highly skilled, among the very best anywhere, the same sense as world-class.

clue.text: One may cut a blunt writer to make a point

definitions.text: One may cut a blunt writer to make a point

parts.words: One may cut a blunt writer to make a point
parts.note: surface reading: someone snubs a plain-spoken author in order to win an argument
setter's reading: the writer is a writing implement with a worn tip, and the device shaves wood to give it a fresh point

explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is a tool, not a person, 'blunt' is its worn tip, and 'point' is the sharp end rather than an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: This desk gadget shaves the wooden casing and lead of a worn drawing implement until its tip is fine again.

clue.text: Almost get leg in tight eastern garment

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Someone can barely squeeze a leg into a snug Oriental robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' looks like it describes the garment; it means drunk, the anagram signal. The shortened word plus 'leg in' is shuffled, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a woman's light, flimsy dressing gown or nightdress, a piece of clothing.

clue.text: Despite shortage of time, board to sustain troop may be arranged… in case

definitions.note: a phrase describing a thing, standing for an adjective

parts.note: a pack is a troop of Cub Scouts or Brownies

indicators.note: a shortage means something is missing, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a board is a table, as in 'board and lodging'
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Though time is short, a committee arranges support for a troop of scouts, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the board sits under the troop and so sustains it. 'In case' looks like 'just in case' but means inside a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something packable can be folded or fitted neatly into luggage, so it may be stowed in a suitcase.

clue.text: Force denied presence of women in crew

indicators.note: being denied someone's presence means going without them, so a letter is removed

parts.note: weight is the downward force of gravity on a mass
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A rowing club refuses to have women in the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In crew' reads as part of the exclusion story, but 'in' only joins, and the crew is a racing boat's team of oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing an eight is a racing boat with eight oarsmen, and the word also names its team of rowers.

clue.text: Bet uncrowned former prince makes comeback before decade's end

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way you came, so the letters run backwards
a crown sits on top, so taking it off loses the opening letter

parts.note: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort

indicators.note: the end is the final part, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A wager that a deposed prince will return to power before the decade is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncrowned' fits a deposed royal, but it strips the first letter from the prince; the rest is turned round before decade's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble is a wager on three selections, all of which must win, a kind of accumulator bet.

clue.text: Troubled Republican in suit misleads in all prime respects

indicators.note: a word placed in something sits inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a suit is slang for a business executive, an exec
R is the abbreviation for Republican

indicators.note: prime positions are the second, third, fifth and seventh, so only letters at those places count

parts.note: letters 2, 3, 5 and 7 of the word

explanation.surface: A Republican in trouble, facing a lawsuit, deceives on every important point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like a lawsuit but is a corporate executive; 'prime' means letters at prime-numbered positions, not the best ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exercised about something is to be worried, agitated or disturbed by it, so the word means upset.

clue.text: One in the know drives a van to stores

indicators.note: to store something is to keep it inside, so the letters are held within the phrase

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the next two, and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone well informed drives a delivery van to the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stores' looks like shops, the van's destination; it is a verb, the phrase storing the answer inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned person with deep knowledge, so someone who knows a great deal.

clue.text: Tense sort of geek fined

indicators.note: to sort things is to rearrange them, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nervy kind of nerd has been handed a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like the geek's mood or even a grammar term; it is the definition, as in a knife-edge finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife-edge situation is precariously balanced and nerve-racking, with the outcome uncertain, so it is tense.

clue.text: Runners moving down south make contact

indicators.note: in a down answer moving down means going to the bottom, so a letter shifts to the end

parts.note: skis are the runners a skier glides on
S is the abbreviation for south; it names which letter moves

explanation.surface: Athletes running downhill to the south meet up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' look like athletes, but they are the blades on snow; their first S drops to the foot of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two balls kiss in snooker or billiards when they lightly touch, so the verb can mean touching.

clue.text: Withdraw from relations backing first wife?

parts.note: a first wife, after a divorce, may be called an ex
it is slang for sex, sexual relations

explanation.surface: Pull out of a family that is siding with the first wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like family but means sex, IT; in a down answer it sits beneath the former wife and so backs her. The question mark flags that an ex is only one kind of first wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit a place or arrangement is to leave or pull out of it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Gutted Aston Villa over halfway to getting a hammering here?

indicators.note: going just past the middle leaves a little more than half, so the tail is cut
gutting removes the insides, so only the outer letters survive

parts.note: the first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Aston Villa fans are gutted to be losing heavily at half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is an English football club, and 'gutted' is British slang for devastated. Three of Villa's five letters is just over half.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith beats hot metal on an anvil, so it is the place where things are struck by hammers.

clue.text: Landslide hasn't spoilt special archipelago

indicators.note: something spoilt is ruined and messed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the apostrophe
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A landslide has not wrecked a particular group of islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoilt' sits between the fodder and S, so it is easy to miss that S must join the shuffle too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shetland Islands are a group of islands far north of mainland Scotland, which is what an archipelago is.
